author: BBC News
description:
Countries have failed to reach a major new deal to tackle climate change after deep divisions over fossil fuels and money emerged at the UN COP31 talks in Turkey. 
 
Negotiations were due to finish on Friday but ran late into Sunday in search of common ground, becoming the longest UN climate conference in history. 
 
But the final deal proved unacceptable to the EU, Pacific island nations and others because it failed to directly mention fossil fuels, the main cause of global warming.
 
Meanwhile, many poorer countries objected to the absence of any clear financial commitments from richer nations to help them adapt to the impacts of rising temperatures.

description:
Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond. The former Twilight star and Batman actor will take on one of cinema’s most scrutinised and iconic roles, after a five year search.

But the bigger story may be who’s making the decisions behind the scenes, Jeff Bezos says he was "'heavily involved" in the casting, but will he continue to influence the production?

Is Pattinson an inspired choice, or a safe one? And as Amazon takes control of the franchise, can 007 stay quintessentially British?

In this episode Tristan Redman hears from our producer Xandra Ellin, who explains Pattinson’s journey from teen heart-throb to Bond. We also revisit our earlier report on Amazon’s purchase of the franchise, with Wall Street Journal enterprise reporter Erich Schwartzel.

Former UK prime ministers including Brexit negotiations veteran Theresa May have been giving their verdicts on Andy Burnham’s UK-EU reset deal.

Laura, Paddy and Henry at home discuss whether their interventions will weigh on Andy Burnham’s mind.

description:
Nations at the COP31 climate talks in Turkey have failed to agree a deal after the EU and others rejected the final agreement.

Australian minister Chris Bowen, COP31's president of negotiations, says the summit faced the "most complicated and fraught geopolitical environment in living memory”.
 
This year’s COP summit in Turkey is the longest-running in history, with negotiations continuing two days after it had been due to end.

description:
Ageing is often viewed as an unavoidable part of life - and death - but Aubrey de Grey believes it should be treated as a medical condition that can be cured, thus extending our lives potentially by hundreds of years.

The gerontologist tells Gabriel Gatehouse how close he thinks we are to future generations routinely living far longer than people do today, and why the first person to reach the age of 1,000 may already have been born. And they discuss what a world of dramatically extended lifespans might be like.

The comedian and author Bob Mortimer gives BBC Media and Arts Correspondent David Sillito a tour of his home town.

Then he heads to a home crowd at the Middlesbrough Town Hall to discuss his new novel 'Michael', which is based on the events of his childhood.

description:
The disability benefit Personal Independence Payment, also known as Pip, is being looked at by disability minister Sir Stephen Timms as part of a review into whether Pip is fit for purpose.
 
The number of people claiming Pip in England and Wales has risen by 46% over the last five years and it has become one of the biggest political battles in welfare.
 
But who was the benefit designed to help and how are people assessed for it?

The BBC’s senior disability correspondent Nikki Fox explains.

author: BBC News
description:
Negotiations at the COP31 UN climate summit in Turkey are in deadlock and have been suspended for the night, after running more than a day over time, as countries have been unable to agree on a new global climate deal.
 
The EU and Pacific island nations are amongst a group pushing back against the latest draft agreement which included no reference to reducing the world's demand for fossil fuels.
 
Negotiating teams due to fly out on Sunday morning are now moving their flights to Monday in a sign that a deal is not yet in sight.
